newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to develop oil palm plantation in Irian.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to develop oil palm plantation in Irian.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned plantations will form a consortium to develop a 102,000-hectare oil palm plantation in Irian Jaya with investments of about one trillion rupiah, local media reported on Thursday.
The reports said the project would also involve the setting up of 11 palm oil refineries.

Bisnis Indonesia newspaper quoted Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah as saying 35 percent of the cost would be met by profits made by the planatations while the rest would be raised from bank loans.

The Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper said the Irian project would be developed over 10 years. It quoted Sofyan Raz, head of one of the plantations, as saying the Irian project would yield 606,000 tonnes of crude palm oil and palm kernel oil yearly.
Raz said he hoped the Irian venture would spur private sector investment in eastern Indonesia, where the lack of infrastructure and other facilities had hindered investments.
